The must-sees

  • Alte Feste

    Fortress · 1890

    German colonial troops began it in 1890 as their headquarters. For decades it housed the national history museum.

  • Christuskirche

    Church · 1910

    Built from local quartz sandstone and consecrated in 1910, it mixes neo-Romanesque and Art Nouveau. The stained-glass windows were a gift from Kaiser Wilhelm II.

    Look for: Inside, plaques name German soldiers killed in the colonial wars of 1904–1908. The far greater number of Herero and Nama dead are not named.

  • Heroes’ Acre

    Landmark · 2002

    Inaugurated on Heroes’ Day 2002, it honours those who fought colonialism and apartheid. A bronze Unknown Soldier and a tall obelisk look out over the Auas Mountains.

    Look for: Below the obelisk, rows of tombs honour named heroes, among them anti-colonial leaders such as Hendrik Witbooi and Samuel Maharero.

  • Independence Memorial Museum

    Museum · 2014

    Built by a North Korean firm and opened in 2014, it is often likened to a coffee pot. Outside, a statue of Sam Nujoma and a memorial to the 1904–1908 genocide of the Herero and Nama.

  • Katutura

    Neighbourhood · 1959

    Black residents were forcibly moved here from the Old Location from 1959. The Otjiherero name means the place where we do not want to live; today it is full of markets, music and street life.

    Look for: At Single Quarters market, look for kapana: strips of beef grilled over open fires and eaten on the spot with spicy salt.

  • Tintenpalast

    Civic building · 1913

    Completed in 1913 as the colonial administration building, it earned its nickname from the amount of ink spent inside. Since 1990 it has housed the National Assembly.

    Look for: In the gardens in front stand statues of leaders who resisted colonial rule, among them Hendrik Witbooi, the Nama chief who fought the Germans.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Windhoek and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Windhoek passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
